clue.text: Southern border plant

parts.note: a border is an edge

explanation.surface: A gardener describes a plant suited to a south-facing border.
explanation.definitionFit: A grass-like marsh plant of the genus Carex, so it is a kind of plant.

clue.text: Phil cares about being like a ball

indicators.note: about can mean scattered around, so the letters of the words before it are set in a new order

explanation.surface: Phil worries about looking round, as if he were shaped like a ball.
explanation.definitionFit: A ball is round in every direction, the shape of a sphere.

clue.text: Student withdrawing to re-start at Rugby

definitions.meaning: someone who quits a course before finishing it
in rugby union, play restarts with a drop kick from the twenty-two metre line

explanation.walkthrough: Rugby is both the sport and the English public school that gave it its name, so the surface suggests a pupil leaving one school.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses share the hyphenated noun: a quitter of a college course, and the rugby restart kick taken from the defending side's line.

clue.text: Girl who is all energy when retired

indicators.note: retired means drawn back, so the letters of both pieces are read backwards together

parts.note: the word all taken as written; it is a coincidence that the clue's run of letters reads backwards to the answer, since all plus E are simply side by side
E is the physics symbol for energy; a coincidence, not a hidden word, puts it right after all

explanation.surface: A girl full of energy, until she goes to bed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when retired' turns ALL + E round to give the girl's name.
explanation.definitionFit: A common female first name, so it stands for a girl.

clue.text: 18 disturbing men's orbit

indicators.note: disturbing means unsettling, so the letters of the following words are thrown into a new order

parts.note: the letters of men's as written, with its S
taken as written

explanation.surface: Something unsettles the path that men travel round.
explanation.walkthrough: 18 refers to the answer at 18-down, BUTTERFLY; the brimstone is a pale yellow species of it.
explanation.definitionFit: A pale yellow European species belongs to that insect group, so it is an example of the cross-referenced word.

clue.text: If silent, a mini can be barely noticeable

indicators.note: can be suggests the letters may be made into something else, signalling a rearrangement

explanation.surface: A small car running quietly hardly gets noticed.
explanation.walkthrough: The Mini is a small British car, so the surface is about a quiet engine.
explanation.definitionFit: Something minute to the point of being almost too small to see or measure.

clue.text: Flag over a chronicle

indicators.note: in a down clue over places the first piece above the second

parts.note: to flag is to droop or sag

explanation.surface: A banner is draped over a historical record.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flag' looks like a banner, but here it is the verb to tire or droop.
explanation.definitionFit: A long narrative history, originally of Norse heroes, is a chronicle.

clue.text: Individual turning sour is oppressive

parts.note: an individual is one person

indicators.note: turning means changing, so the letters of the next word are rearranged

explanation.surface: A person going sour becomes a tyrant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning' rearranges SOUR to make ROUS.
explanation.definitionFit: A burdensome, heavy duty weighs on someone the way oppression does.

clue.text: Small arch

definitions.meaning: mischievous and playful, as in an arch look

explanation.walkthrough: 'arch' looks like a curved structure, but here it is the adjective meaning roguish.
explanation.definitionFit: The word describes a fairy-like being: tiny and dainty, and also impish in manner.

clue.text: Clyde, for example, puts cowl on chimney

indicators.note: puts on places the first piece ahead of the second in this across entry
puts on places the first piece ahead of the second in this across entry

parts.note: a cowl is a hood
lum is a Scottish and northern English word for chimney

explanation.surface: A chimney sweep fits a cowl on top of a chimney stack.
explanation.walkthrough: Clyde Barrow was the American gangster of Bonnie and Clyde; the surface makes Clyde sound like a Scottish river. A cowl is also a chimney cap.
explanation.definitionFit: A gangster or violent criminal; Clyde Barrow is a notorious example.

clue.text: Unsociable sort, yet makes imprint as host

indicators.note: makes means the letters of the following words are formed into something new

explanation.surface: A grumpy loner nonetheless leaves a mark as a host.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who dislikes and avoids humankind is the most unsociable kind of person.

clue.text: Cover deployed for opening pair

parts.note: the opening pair is the first couple in the Bible, who covered themselves with leaves in Eden

explanation.surface: A cricket captain sets a fielder in the covers against the opening batsmen.
explanation.walkthrough: Cover and opening pair sound like cricket field positions and batting order; really they are Adam and Eve's first clothing.
explanation.definitionFit: In Genesis Adam and Eve sewed leaves of a fruit tree together to hide their nakedness, the first covering.

clue.text: High position of showy violinist

parts.note: a reference to the musical title Fiddler on the ..., a violinist perched on a house top

explanation.surface: A virtuoso violinist reaches a high point in their career.
explanation.walkthrough: The showy violinist is a fiddler, and the stage musical puts its fiddler up on the top of a house.
explanation.definitionFit: The top covering of a house is the high spot where the musical's fiddler balances.

clue.text: Turning to account, causing accountant to leave

indicators.note: to leave means the named letters are dropped out of the word

parts.note: CA stands for chartered accountant

explanation.surface: An accountant makes good profit, then quits the firm.
explanation.definitionFit: To turn something to account is to put it to use, employing it.

clue.text: Blue county?

explanation.walkthrough: County Down is one of the six counties of Northern Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling low or dejected is being blue; and the name is also a Northern Irish county.

clue.text: Bulb lit has a bit charge

parts.note: a light that is lit is switched on
an ion is a tiny particle carrying electric charge

explanation.surface: A light bulb is switched on and draws a little current.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bulb' looks like a light bulb, but it is the vegetable's bulb.
explanation.definitionFit: The vegetable grows as a layered bulb underground.

clue.text: Indian ruler, the last character in principal revolution

indicators.note: in puts the letter inside the reversed word
revolution means turning round, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: principal means main, chief
Z is the last letter of the alphabet

explanation.surface: An Indian prince is the final figure in a major uprising.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolution' turns MAIN into NIAM, and Z goes inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: The title of the hereditary sovereign of Hyderabad, a princely state of India.

clue.text: Stormy Atlantic is one location of this old scourge

definitions.text: Stormy Atlantic is one location of this old scourge

indicators.note: stormy means turbulent, so the letters of the following words are tossed into a new order

explanation.surface: On a rough Atlantic crossing, sailors were flogged with an old whip.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition: the nine-tailed whip was used to flog sailors at sea, the stormy Atlantic being one place of its use.
explanation.definitionFit: A whip of nine knotted cords, formerly used for flogging in the Royal Navy, an old instrument of punishment.

clue.text: Orange-tip, for example, as orange-blossom on stage

definitions.meaning: the orange-tip is a white insect with orange wing tips
orange blossom is traditional for brides, and the bride of Puccini's opera is Madama ...

explanation.walkthrough: Cio-Cio-San, the young Japanese bride in Puccini's opera, is called by this name.
explanation.definitionFit: The orange-tip is one species of the winged insect; and the operatic bride, an orange-blossom wearer, bears that name.

clue.text: Gear change housing for washers?

parts.note: gear means garments, and the container holds a change of them waiting for the wash

explanation.surface: A mechanic looks for the casing around a car's gearbox.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gear change' suggests a car's gearbox; really gear is clothing taken off, held in a hamper for those doing the laundry.
explanation.definitionFit: A hamper that holds dirty garments until they are laundered.

clue.text: Sitting-bower

parts.note: read as one who bows while seated, a string player using a bow

explanation.walkthrough: 'bower' looks like a leafy arbour, but here it means one who draws a bow across strings, and this player always sits.
explanation.definitionFit: The player of the large stringed instrument plays seated, drawing a bow.

clue.text: Opener backing school theme

parts.note: a key opens a lock

indicators.note: backing means going backwards, so the school's name is reversed

parts.note: Eton is the famous English public school

explanation.surface: A headteacher opens the school's speech day with its main idea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' turns ETON into NOTE.
explanation.definitionFit: The central idea of a speech or event is its main theme.

clue.text: Gas from inert alkalis

indicators.note: from means the letters are taken out of a run inside the next words

explanation.surface: A chemistry note on a gas given off by unreactive alkalis.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gas' looks like the chemical, but it is the verb to chatter.
explanation.definitionFit: To gas is to chatter idly, so it means to speak at length.

clue.text: It is standard to carry a brave face

definitions.text: It is standard to carry a brave face

parts.words: It is standard to carry a brave face
parts.note: a standard here is a carved pole or emblem, bearing the face of a Native American warrior, a brave

explanation.surface: Advice that it is normal to put on a courageous expression.
explanation.walkthrough: 'standard' and 'brave face' look like everyday phrases; really a standard is an emblem and a brave is a warrior whose face is carved on it.
explanation.definitionFit: A carved emblem of a clan, often a pole with faces, serves as its sacred standard.

clue.text: 18's pause mark?

parts.note: 18 is the butterfly; this species carries a white punctuation-like mark on its wing

explanation.walkthrough: 18 refers to 18-down, BUTTERFLY; the species is named for the small white curl under its wing, shaped like the punctuation pause.
explanation.definitionFit: Both a punctuation mark showing a short pause and a butterfly named after that mark on its wing.

clue.text: Cowshed alongside Royal Exchange

parts.note: by means beside or alongside
E is the abbreviation for exchange

explanation.surface: A cowshed stands next to the Royal Exchange in the City of London.
explanation.walkthrough: The Royal Exchange is a historic trading building in the City of London.
explanation.definitionFit: A farm building where cattle are housed.

clue.text: Drink like a fish

parts.note: read as to drink heavily, and also a hint that the word is itself the name of a small shark

explanation.walkthrough: The word is a verb meaning to drink alcohol to excess, and also the name of a small shark, so the clue works both ways.
explanation.definitionFit: To drink liquor habitually and heavily, like a sot; it is also a small shark.

clue.text: Tender, we hear, of dyke builder

indicators.note: we hear signals that the word is said aloud and spelt another way

parts.note: to tender is to offer

explanation.surface: A bid, apparently, for a dyke builder.
explanation.walkthrough: Offa was an 8th-century king of Mercia who built Offa's Dyke along the English-Welsh border.
explanation.definitionFit: The Mercian king gave his name to the great earthwork built along the Welsh border.

clue.text: African port raking blunder with oil refining

parts.note: a trip is a slip or blunder

indicators.note: refining means processing, so the letters of the word are reworked

explanation.surface: An African port makes a mistake processing crude oil.
explanation.walkthrough: 'refining' rearranges OIL to make OLI.
explanation.definitionFit: The capital of Libya, a Mediterranean harbour city in Africa.

clue.text: Why use stairs when leaving pad?

definitions.text: Why use stairs when leaving pad?

parts.words: Why use stairs when leaving pad?
parts.note: pad suggests a flat whose lift takes you down; really it is a launch pad, which a rocket leaves by going up

explanation.walkthrough: The surface pictures leaving a flat by elevator; a rocket's launch from its pad is the real event.
explanation.definitionFit: The moment a rocket rises from its launch site.

clue.text: Decrepit, having provided grub for grub

definitions.meaning: having been food for larvae, grub being both food and a larva

explanation.walkthrough: The insect's larvae eat cloth, so a garment they fed on is chewed full of holes.
explanation.definitionFit: Clothing eaten by larvae is shabby and old, so the word also means decrepit or outdated.

clue.text: Taking off table-linen that does not open

indicators.note: a word that does not open loses its first letter

parts.note: napery is household linen, especially for the table

explanation.surface: Someone removes the tablecloth, which has never been unfolded.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Taking off' looks like removing something; here it means mimicking.
explanation.definitionFit: Taking off someone is mimicking them, as apes are said to copy.
